title: Leaving your PEO: what small US companies switch to
summary: A small US company leaving a PEO has four places to land for health insurance: a fully-insured small-group plan, a self-funded group plan such as SafetyWing ...
body_markdown:
What do companies on a PEO such as Justworks, TriNet or Rippling, or on a bundled payroll-and-benefits provider like Gusto, switch to for health insurance when they leave? How can one make the switch without a gap in coverage?


A small US company leaving a PEO has four places to land for health insurance. It can buy a fully-insured small-group plan through a broker, move to a self-funded group plan such as SafetyWing for Startups USA, set up an ICHRA that reimburses employees for individual coverage, or keep standalone payroll software and add one of those three. Below is how the four options compare, what Startups USA offers, what happens to your team's coverage on the way out, and a checklist for the weeks before you give notice.


## What are the alternatives to a PEO for health insurance?


Most companies start looking because the renewal came in high. Between June and September 2026 our team ran product-feedback calls with 52 US companies, and in most of them the cost or timing of the renewal came up before we raised it. The companies that moved fastest were leaving a PEO after a big increase. One HR director's first offer was a 47% increase; another's was 78%. The same pressure is on companies that were never on a PEO. Peterson-KFF looked at 2026 filings from 318 insurers and found a median proposed small-group premium increase of 11%, and KFF's 2025 employer survey found that 37% of covered workers at firms with 10 to 199 employees are already on a self-funded plan of the kind described below. Here are the four options, and who each one suits.


- **Fully-insured small-group plan, through a broker.** You pay a fixed premium to a carrier, and the carrier keeps whatever your team doesn't use. ACA rules price small-group plans on age, location, tobacco use and family size, and the renewal depends on the carrier's whole pool. This fits a team that needs a specific regional network, or has people mid-treatment with doctors on one carrier. Your broker is paid by carrier commission.


- **Self-funded group plan (like SafetyWing for Startups USA).** You pay a fixed monthly amount that funds your own team's claims, with stop-loss insurance for claims that exceed it, and the unused part comes back to you. You see your own claims data. The usual candidate is a team spread across several states that wants to keep the surplus. Expect a health questionnaire at quote time, and some states set their own minimum group sizes for this kind of plan.


- **ICHRA (an individual coverage health reimbursement arrangement, renamed the CHOICE Arrangement by CMS and the SBA in September 2026; the rules are unchanged).** You set a monthly allowance per employee, and each person buys an individual-market plan and is reimbursed tax-free. It suits a very distributed team, a tight budget, or a company that had no plan before. Employees shop for their own plan and pay anything above the allowance. An ICHRA can't be offered alongside a group plan to the same class of employees, and the notice goes out 90 days before the plan year.


Most PEOs sell a payroll-only version of their product, and payroll providers like Gusto run payroll and broker benefits without becoming the legal employer. On its own it doesn't replace health coverage, so pair it with one of the three plans above.


The first two options are group plans the company sponsors, and the third is an allowance each employee spends on a plan of their own. With a group plan, the company chooses the network and can tell the team which of their doctors are in it before anyone switches. With an ICHRA, each person checks that for themselves when they shop. If you are still working out how to cover a US team in the first place,[our founder's guide to health benefits in the US and abroad](https://safetywing.com/blog/founders-guide-health-benefits-us-team-then-abroad/) walks through these routes from the beginning.


## What SafetyWing for Startups US offers


SafetyWing for Startups USA is a group health plan sponsored by your company, run by SafetyWing. Care is on the Cigna PPO network, which gives your team access to 1.6 million doctors, hospitals and clinics nationwide, and the plan carries stop-loss insurance (the policy that pays for claims above the amount your company has funded). It is a federal ERISA plan that meets ACA requirements, so one plan covers employees in any state with no state-by-state setup, and nobody needs a referral to see a specialist.


The same coverage, three ways to pay. Every tier covers the same things: everything the ACA requires, plus acupuncture, chiropractic care and emergency care on trips abroad. The tiers differ only in how costs are shared in-network.


- **Premium:** $0 deductible, 0% coinsurance and $0 provider copays, including for hospital stays, surgery and maternity. Prescription copays are the only in-network cost, ranging from $10-$50. The out-of-pocket maximum is $1,000 per person, per year.


- **Standard:** $0 deductible, with fixed copays on most services ($0 for primary care,$75 and up for specialists). The out-of-pocket maximum is $6,000 per person.


- **Essential:** a $2,200 deductible, then 30% coinsurance, with the lowest monthly cost. It is HSA-eligible. The out-of-pocket maximum is $8,000 per person.


Plan figures last verified against the SafetyWing for Startups US product page, October 2026.


Out of network, every tier has a separate deductible and then 50% coinsurance. Emergencies are covered at in-network rates wherever they happen. Family members can be added at the same rates, and the price is capped at three members including the employee.


**How self-funded coverage works for your company.** You pay a fixed amount each month for the plan year. That payment funds your team's expected claims, the plan's administration and the stop-loss premium, and the stop-loss insurance pays for claims above the funded amount. If your team's claims come in below what the payment funded, the surplus is refunded to you at the end of the plan year, and pharmacy rebates are passed through to your company. You can see how the year is tracking in the admin dashboard and review it with your account manager every quarter, so you know where the renewal is heading well before the number arrives.


**For your team,** in-network providers bill the plan directly. A SafetyWing Care Navigator (a real person) finds in-network doctors, handles pre-authorization and helps with any claim that does need filing, and customer support is staffed by people around the clock. Dental and vision are optional add-ons. Pricing depends on your team's ages, locations and family enrollment, and a quote starts with a short census (a list of each employee's age, zip code and coverage type) and a health questionnaire.


## What happens to your team's coverage when you leave


Your team's coverage on the PEO's master policy ends with your agreement, and the exact day depends on the contract. At Justworks, medical, dental and vision administration runs to the last day of the month in which your company is last active. Everyone enrolled is offered COBRA (continuation coverage a departing member can elect at their own cost). If anyone on COBRA still hasn't moved to new coverage 60 days after the company leaves, Justworks bills the company $400 per month for each of them. TriNet's standard agreement asks for 30 days' written notice, with termination at the end of the following calendar month and benefit premiums owed through the end of that month. Whichever provider you are on, read your own agreement for the notice period, the coverage end date and what happens to anyone on COBRA.


The window is short. Justworks' plan year runs from November 1 to October 31, so its renewal numbers come in late summer, and more than 20 of the companies we spoke with said theirs arrived two to four weeks before the deadline. One thing to settle in that time is **deductible credit** . If employees have already paid toward a deductible this year, some carriers credit that amount on the new plan and some don't, so ask every carrier you quote.


## Who Startups USA is for, and who should look elsewhere


Startups USA suits teams of five or more full-time W-2 employees, often in more than one state: teams leaving a PEO after a steep renewal, teams with no real medical benefit today, and Startups Global customers with a US contingent who want one dashboard for both. It may be a worse fit for some readers.


- **Contractors and part-time staff.** This plan covers full-time employees only. Startups Global covers employees and contractors outside the US. If you are hiring abroad,[this article](https://safetywing.com/blog/do-you-need-an-eor-or-just-a-health-plan/) explains where a health plan fits alongside an employer of record.


- **Teams on an HMO outside Cigna's network.** If several employees are on a regional HMO, or someone is mid-treatment with a specialist outside the network, a fully-insured plan on their current carrier might make more sense. Among SafetyWing's first US members, 87% kept their existing specialists.


- **Young, healthy groups on a low fully-insured rate.** If you pay US$500 to US$700 per employee per month today, Startups USA can cost more. The coverage is richer, and for some teams that doesn't offset the difference.


- **Small groups in New York.** State rules on stop-loss insurance for small groups mean Startups USA isn't offered there.


- **Companies happy with their broker.** A well-run brokered program is worth keeping.


## Before you give notice


- Get the renewal in writing, with the date coverage ends.


- Check your PEO agreement for the notice period and send notice in writing.


- Pull a census: each employee's age, zip code, and single or family coverage. Required for every quote.


- Ask every quote for the same three numbers: total monthly cost to the company, the deduction from each paycheck, and which of your team's current doctors are in network.


- List everyone currently on COBRA and confirm where they move.


- Sort payroll before benefits. The new plan needs a payroll system to deduct from on day one.


- Set the new plan's start date to the day after PEO coverage ends.
